title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
byline: Guo, Yang, Zhang and colleagues, DeepSeek-AI, 2025
gist: The paper trains reasoning models by applying reinforcement learning directly to a base language model without supervised demonstration data. It then uses the discovered reasoning traces to train smaller dense models through distillation.

problem.text: Human reasoning demonstrations are expensive to curate and introduce human cognitive biases. Supervised fine-tuning encourages models to imitate human solutions rather than explore better reasoning paths. Standard demonstrations also omit self-correction and verification steps. These factors cap model performance on complex problems.

newIdea.text: A raw base language model can develop multi-step reasoning, self-reflection, and verification entirely through outcome-based reinforcement learning without an initial supervised fine-tuning stage.

claims.text: Pure reinforcement learning applied to a base model induces chain-of-thought behaviors such as self-verification, backtracking, and longer thinking time without human demonstrations.
Group Relative Policy Optimization removes the need for a separate value model by estimating baseline advantages directly from group rewards, reducing memory and compute costs.
A multi-stage pipeline combining cold-start data, reinforcement learning, rejection sampling, and preference tuning resolves language mixing and poor readability without sacrificing reasoning.

Reasoning trajectories from large reinforcement-learning models can be distilled into smaller models with supervised fine-tuning, exceeding the performance of reinforcement learning on those smaller models.

method.detail: Train DeepSeek-V3-Base using Group Relative Policy Optimization without prior supervised fine-tuning. Apply rule-based rewards based on answer accuracy and format compliance.
Generate reasoning trajectories using the initial checkpoint and human examples. Filter out mixed-language outputs and prompt DeepSeek-V3 to produce human-readable first-person reasoning.
Fine-tune DeepSeek-V3-Base on cold-start data and train it with reinforcement learning. Add a language consistency reward proportional to target language words in the reasoning trace.
Sample candidate solutions from the RL checkpoint using rejection sampling. Merge 600,000 verified reasoning examples with 200,000 non-reasoning examples to train the model for two epochs.
Train for 1,700 steps using rule-based rewards for reasoning tasks. Apply neural reward models for helpfulness and safety during the final 400 steps with sampling temperature at 0.7.
Fine-tune open base models including Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 on the curated 800,000 supervised trajectories for two to three epochs without an active reinforcement learning stage.

findings.text: DeepSeek-R1-Zero increases its AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy from 15.6% to 77.9% during reinforcement learning, and reaches 86.7% through consensus voting over 64 samples.
DeepSeek-R1 achieves 79.8% pass@1 on AIME 2024, 97.3% on MATH-500, and a 2029 rating at the 96.3 percentile on Codeforces.
On AIME 2025, DeepSeek-R1 attains a 75% pass@1 solve rate, and achieves a score of 143.7 out of 150 on AMC 12 2024.
Distilling the 800,000 samples into Qwen2.5-32B yields 72.6% pass@1 on AIME 2024, whereas training Qwen2.5-32B directly with reinforcement learning yields 47.0%.
Training DeepSeek-R1-Zero used 101,000 H800 GPU hours ($202,000), DeepSeek-R1 used 41,000 H800 GPU hours ($82,000), and SFT dataset creation used 5,000 GPU hours ($10,000).

limitations.text: Pure reinforcement learning requires reliable reward signals, which are difficult to construct for subjective tasks such as creative writing without causing reward hacking.
The model lacks integration with tools such as calculators or web search, and exhibits suboptimal performance on structured output formatting.
The model exhibits token inefficiency through excessive thinking on simple queries, and few-shot prompting degrades performance relative to zero-shot prompting.
The model mixes languages when prompted in languages other than Chinese and English because pre-training data is predominantly Chinese and English.
Dense models with 7B parameters and mixture-of-experts models with 16B parameters failed to develop long chain-of-thought reasoning during pure reinforcement learning.

related.label: GRPO

related.link: GRPO defines the reinforcement learning algorithm used across both training phases of DeepSeek-R1. It replaces the critic model in standard policy gradient methods with group-normalized scores.

related.link: PPO is the standard policy optimization algorithm in language model alignment. DeepSeek-R1 compares against it to demonstrate the memory and compute benefits of omitting the value model.
carried: Clipped probability ratio objective to constrain policy drift
Optimization using multiple rollout generations per prompt
changed: PPO trains a separate value network equal to policy size
PPO penalizes per-token KL divergence in the reward

openDirections.label: Tool-Integrated RL
openDirections.title: Embedding external code execution and search directly into policy training
openDirections.shows: DeepSeek-R1 operates without external tools, relying entirely on internal token generation for arithmetic, retrieval, and code validation.
openDirections.open: The paper does not test whether adding tool calling actions into group policy optimization disrupts the emergence of internal self-reflection.
openDirections.move: Add python interpreter tags into the GRPO action space on math tasks that exceed 64-bit integer precision and compare reasoning length.

openDirections.label: Adaptive Token Budgets
openDirections.title: Controlling token waste on simple tasks without degrading hard problem solving
openDirections.shows: DeepSeek-R1 scales test-time compute dynamically with task complexity, but overthinks simpler questions like basic arithmetic.
openDirections.open: It remains untested whether an explicit token budget reward penalty can curb verbosity on simple inputs without suppressing reflection on hard inputs.
openDirections.move: Train a checkpoint with an added reward penalty proportional to generated tokens for inputs classified below a difficulty threshold.

openDirections.label: Hybrid Verifier Signals
openDirections.title: Combining outcome verification with formal automated intermediate checks
openDirections.shows: Neural process reward models suffered from reward hacking, forcing the authors to rely exclusively on final outcome rewards.
openDirections.open: Whether formal deterministic step checkers, such as interactive theorem prover steps, avoid the hacking observed in learned reward models.
openDirections.move: Evaluate GRPO using formal Lean theorem proving environments where intermediate proof steps provide deterministic binary feedback.

openDirections.label: Small Model Direct RL
openDirections.title: Inducing long chain-of-thought behaviors directly in sub-10B base checkpoints
openDirections.shows: Direct RL from scratch succeeded on 32B dense and 671B MoE base models, but failed on 7B dense and 16B MoE models due to repetitive loops.
openDirections.open: The authors do not isolate whether failure in small models is caused by pre-training token volume, architecture width, or lack of reasoning traces.
openDirections.move: Test GRPO on 7B models pre-trained with varying proportions of synthetic code-execution data to identify the threshold for RL emergence.

glossary.plain: A reinforcement learning algorithm that scores a group of sampled model outputs against their average, removing the need for a separate critic model.
A sequence of intermediate thinking steps generated by a language model before presenting its final answer.
A small curated dataset used to fine-tune a base model into a coherent style before reinforcement learning begins.
Generating multiple candidate outputs from a model and filtering them to retain only those that satisfy verification rules.
A failure mode where a model exploits flaws in a reward function to achieve high scores without fulfilling the intended task.
Training a smaller student model to reproduce the outputs and reasoning trajectories generated by a larger teacher model.
A scoring signal computed by programmatic checks such as exact text matching or test case execution rather than a learned neural network.
An evaluation metric measuring the proportion of problems where a single sampled response is correct.
